title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: The page is an explicit linear-algebra computation. Let ξ1, ξ2, ξ3 be distinct quantities. The next page identifies them as ξ_i = ℘(ε_i), the x-coordinates of the three nonzero 2-torsion points (half-periods) of an elliptic curve in Weierstrass form y² = 4∏(x−ξ_i). The page solves the system ξ_i f1 + f2 = (e_j − e_k)/(ξ_j − ξ_k) for (i,j,k) cyclic, with unknown vectors f1, f2, expressed in terms of vectors e1, e2, e3 in some module. Plausibly f1, f2 are a basis adapted to the Weierstrass description and e1, e2, e3 a basis adapted to the level-2 (Legendre-type) description, for example of a tangent or derivation space on the moduli of curves with level-2 structure; this reading is a guess. It is a 3×2 Vandermonde-type system. Subtracting the first two equations gives (ξ1−ξ2) f1 = e1/(ξ3−ξ1) + e2/(ξ2−ξ3) − (1/(ξ3−ξ1) + 1/(ξ2−ξ3)) e3. The bracket simplifies to (ξ2−ξ1)/((ξ3−ξ1)(ξ2−ξ3)). Back-substitution f2 = (e2−e3)/(ξ2−ξ3) − ξ1 f1 and clearing denominators by Δ0 = (ξ1−ξ2)(ξ2−ξ3)(ξ3−ξ1) give Δ0 f2 = −ξ1(ξ2−ξ3)e1 − ξ2(ξ3−ξ1)e2 − ξ3(ξ1−ξ2)e3. The next page completes this to Δ0 f1 = Σ(ξ_j−ξ_k)e_i and −Δ0 f2 = Σ ξ_i(ξ_j−ξ_k)e_i, then reads the f1-direction as Σ(℘(ε_j)−℘(ε_k))e_i. Δ0 is the square root of the discriminant, up to a constant: Δ = 16Δ0². The page serves the comparison between Weierstrass coordinates (g2, g3) and level-2 coordinates (ξ_i) in Grothendieck's study of the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. The paper is the back of a Montpellier thesis-defence notice dated 4 Nov 1980, so the page dates from after that.
errors: No errors. I checked: the coefficient of e3 in f1 is −(1/(ξ1−ξ2))·(ξ2−ξ1)/((ξ3−ξ1)(ξ2−ξ3)) = (ξ1−ξ2)/Δ0. The e2 coefficient of Δ0 f2 is (ξ3−ξ1)(ξ1−ξ2−ξ1) = −ξ2(ξ3−ξ1). The e3 coefficient of Δ0 f2 is (ξ1−ξ2)(−(ξ3−ξ1)−ξ1) = −ξ3(ξ1−ξ2). The overdetermined system is automatically consistent: the third equation holds for the solution, because the compatibility condition reduces to Σ(e_j − e_k) = 0.
The f1 line leaves the e3 bracket as an empty placeholder '( )'; it is filled implicitly on the next page.

ideas.what: Inversion of a Vandermonde-type linear system relating two bases, with coefficients in the 2-torsion abscissae ξ_i = ℘(ε_i); the denominator is Δ0 = ∏(ξ_i − ξ_j), the square root of the discriminant
ideas.modern_name: Change of coordinates between the Weierstrass (g2, g3) and Legendre/level-2 (e_i = ℘(ω_i/2)) descriptions of elliptic curves; Lagrange interpolation / Vandermonde inversion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass, Legendre, Jacobi; 19th-century elliptic function theory)

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely routine algebra: inverting a small Vandermonde-type system with the half-period values of ℘. It is a calculation step in the unpublished notes on moduli of elliptic curves, with no new concept on the page itself.
transcription_corrections: The final line in the image reads '−ξ1(ξ2−ξ3)e1 − ξ2(ξ3−ξ1)e2 − ξ3(ξ1−ξ2)e3'. The middle sign is an ink blot that the image does not settle; '−' is the algebraically correct value. This line is the simplified form of the preceding bracketed expression for Δ0 f2.
In the f1 line the e3 coefficient is written '−1/(ξ1−ξ2) ( ) e3', with the parenthesis left empty; it refers to the underbraced sum in the line above.
The third equation's left side is ξ3 f1 + f2; the scan's ink makes it look like 'ξ3 f1 − f2'.
